scenes.title: Soldier
scenes.reentry: What business is that of yours? Is it far?

scenes.title: Soldier
scenes.reentry: That’s too far for me. Give me a kiss.

scenes.title: Soldier
scenes.reentry: I don’t. No, I can’t go with you. It’s too far.

scenes.title: Soldier
scenes.reentry: Sure. Give me your address.

scenes.title: Soldier
scenes.reentry: If I promise!

scenes.title: Soldier
scenes.reentry: What’s there?

scenes.title: Soldier
scenes.reentry: Oh, that’s not the real thing.

scenes.title: Soldier
scenes.reentry: Come along then—but quick.

scenes.title: Soldier
scenes.reentry: Would be the best thing, perhaps.

scenes.title: Soldier
scenes.reentry: You seem to know this place pretty well.

scenes.title: Soldier
scenes.reentry: I’d fight too much.

scenes.title: Soldier
scenes.reentry: Humph—

scenes.title: Soldier
scenes.reentry: Come here. Come over here.

scenes.title: Soldier
scenes.reentry: (*Has grabbed her*) Oh you—

scenes.title: Soldier
scenes.reentry: Don’t be afraid…

scenes.title: Girl
scenes.reentry: It would have been nicer on the bench.

scenes.title: Girl
scenes.reentry: What’s your hurry—?

scenes.title: Girl
scenes.reentry: Say, what’s your name?

scenes.title: Girl
scenes.reentry: My name is Leocadia.

scenes.title: Girl
scenes.reentry: Listen!

scenes.title: Girl
scenes.reentry: Give me just a dime for the janitor.

scenes.title: Girl
scenes.reentry: Tightwad! Pimp!

scenes.title: The Soldier and the Parlor-Maid
scenes.reentry: *Prater Gardens. Sunday Evening. A road which leads from the Wurstelprater[1] into dark tree arcades. Confused music from the Wurstelprater can still be heard; also strains from the cheap dancehall, a vulgar polka, played by a brass band. T

scenes.title: Maid
scenes.reentry: Now tell me why you wanted to leave.

scenes.title: Maid
scenes.reentry: It was so beautiful and I so love to dance.

scenes.title: Maid
scenes.reentry: (*Submitting*) But we aren’t dancing now. Why do you hold me so tight?

scenes.title: Maid
scenes.reentry: You’ve always got a “Katy” on your mind.

scenes.title: Maid
scenes.reentry: Goodness, it’s dark here. I’m afraid.

scenes.title: Maid
scenes.reentry: But where are we going? There’s no one around. Come, let’s go back!… It’s so dark!

scenes.title: Soldier
scenes.reentry: (*Pulling at his cigar until it glows brightly*) There … it’s already getting brighter. Ha—! Oh, you dearie!

scenes.title: Maid
scenes.reentry: Oh! what are you doing there? If I had known this before!

scenes.title: Maid
scenes.reentry: Did you find it out in the same way with all the others?

scenes.title: Maid
scenes.reentry: But you danced much oftener with that cross-eyed blonde than with me.

scenes.title: Maid
scenes.reentry: Of the corporal with the upturned mustache?

scenes.title: Maid
scenes.reentry: Oh I know. He’s fresh.

scenes.title: Maid
scenes.reentry: Oh nothing… I only noticed how he was with the others.

scenes.title: Maid
scenes.reentry: You’ll burn me with your cigar.

scenes.title: Maid
scenes.reentry: We’re not such good friends yet…

scenes.title: Maid
scenes.reentry: Next time, if we… But, Frank!

scenes.title: Maid
scenes.reentry: But, Frank…

scenes.title: Maid
scenes.reentry: Don’t be so fresh—but, sh-h, suppose some one should come!

scenes.title: Maid
scenes.reentry: For goodness’ sake, where are we going?

scenes.title: Maid
scenes.reentry: Where? I don’t see anything.

scenes.title: Maid
scenes.reentry: Why do you say: “two like us”—

scenes.title: Maid
scenes.reentry: Look out! What’s that there? I nearly fell.

scenes.title: Maid
scenes.reentry: Don’t shove me so. I’ll fall.

scenes.title: Maid
scenes.reentry: Stop! Now I’m really going to scream—What are you doing?… Stop now—

scenes.title: Maid
scenes.reentry: Then, let’s go back where the people are.

scenes.title: Maid
scenes.reentry: Stop, Frank, please, for Heaven’s sake! Listen to me, if I had … known … oh … come!

scenes.title: Soldier
scenes.reentry: (*Blissfully*) Once more… Oh…

scenes.title: Soldier
scenes.reentry: Don’t matter—my face…

scenes.title: Soldier
scenes.reentry: Well, Miss Marie, you can’t stay here on the grass all night.

scenes.title: Soldier
scenes.reentry: Oh, come along.

scenes.title: Soldier
scenes.reentry: Well, what’s the matter with me?

scenes.title: Soldier
scenes.reentry: Yes, yes. Say, wait a minute.

scenes.title: Soldier
scenes.reentry: Can’t you let me light my cigar!

scenes.title: Soldier
scenes.reentry: It’ll be light again to-morrow morning.

scenes.title: Soldier
scenes.reentry: Well, you must have felt that, Miss Marie!

scenes.title: Soldier
scenes.reentry: Back, of course.

scenes.title: Soldier
scenes.reentry: Well, what’s wrong? I don’t like to walk around in the dark.

scenes.title: Soldier
scenes.reentry: But I just told you that I loved you!

scenes.title: Soldier
scenes.reentry: (*Condescendingly*) There… Listen—There’s the music again.

scenes.title: Soldier
scenes.reentry: Of course, why not?

scenes.title: Soldier
scenes.reentry: Well, you can go home.

scenes.title: Soldier
scenes.reentry: Take you home? Oh!

scenes.title: Soldier
scenes.reentry: Where do you live?

scenes.title: Soldier
scenes.reentry: So? Then we go the same way … but it’s still too early for me … me for the dance… I’ve got late leave to-day… I don’t need to be back at the barracks before twelve o’clock. I’m going to dance.

scenes.title: Maid
scenes.reentry: Oh, I see, now it’s that cross-eyed blonde’s turn.

scenes.title: Maid
scenes.reentry: Oh Lord, how wicked men are. I’m sure you do the same to every one.

scenes.title: Maid
scenes.reentry: Please, Frank, no more to-day—stay with me to-day, you see—

scenes.title: Maid
scenes.reentry: I’m not going to dance with any one else to-night.

scenes.title: Maid
scenes.reentry: What?

scenes.title: Maid
scenes.reentry: Yes, I’ll wait.

scenes.title: Soldier
scenes.reentry: Say, Miss Marie, get yourself a glass of beer. (*Turning to a blonde who is just dancing past him in the arms of another, very formally*) Miss, may I ask for a dance?—

scenes.title: The Parlor Maid and the Young Man
scenes.place: The Parlor Maid and the Young Man
scenes.reentry: *Sultry summer afternoon. The parents of the Young MAN are away in the country. The cook has gone out. The Parlor-Maid is in the kitchen writing a letter to the soldier who is now her sweetheart. The Young MAN’S bell rings. She gets up and

scenes.title: Maid
scenes.reentry: Yes, Sir?

scenes.title: Young Man
scenes.reentry: (*Continues reading*) What are you doing, Marie? Oh, yes. But, now, I can’t see to read.

scenes.title: Maid
scenes.reentry: You are always so studious, Sir.

scenes.title: Young Man
scenes.reentry: (*Tries to go on with his reading, lets the book fall, and rings again*)

scenes.title: (Enters)
scenes.reentry: Young MAN

scenes.title: Maid
scenes.reentry: Yes, but it’s locked up.

scenes.title: Maid
scenes.reentry: Lini.

scenes.title: Maid
scenes.reentry: The cook, Mr. Alfred.

scenes.title: Maid
scenes.reentry: Yes, but it’s Lini’s day out.

scenes.title: Maid
scenes.reentry: Can I get anything for you from the café, Sir?

scenes.title: Young Man
scenes.reentry: Thank you—Well, what is the matter?—Be careful. Put the glass back on the tray. (*He leans back, and stretches himself*) How late is it?

scenes.title: Maid
scenes.reentry: Five o’clock, Sir.

scenes.title: Maid
scenes.reentry: (*Goes. At the door she turns around. The Young MAN has followed her with his eyes; she notices it, and smiles*)

scenes.title: Young Man
scenes.reentry: (*Remains stretched out awhile; then, suddenly, he gets up. He walks to the door, back again, and lies down on the couch. He again tries to read. After a few moments, he rings once more.*)

scenes.title: Maid
scenes.reentry: (*Appears with a smile which she does not try to hide*)

scenes.title: Maid
scenes.reentry: No, Sir, nobody called this morning.

scenes.title: Maid
scenes.reentry: Of course, I do. He’s the big gentleman with the black beard.

scenes.title: Maid
scenes.reentry: No, Sir. Nobody called.

scenes.title: Maid
scenes.reentry: (*Coming a little nearer*) Yes, Sir.

scenes.title: Maid
scenes.reentry: Do you want anything, Sir?

scenes.title: Maid
scenes.reentry: (*Comes close to him*) What is the matter with my blouse? Don’t you like it, Sir?

scenes.title: Young Man
scenes.reentry: (*Takes hold of her blouse, and draws her down to him*) Blue? It is a nice blue. (*Simply*) You are very prettily dressed, Marie.

scenes.title: Maid
scenes.reentry: But, Sir…

scenes.title: Maid
scenes.reentry: You are flattering me, Sir.

scenes.title: Maid
scenes.reentry: Oh, no.

scenes.title: Maid
scenes.reentry: Oh, Mr. Alfred…

scenes.title: Maid
scenes.reentry: … But … Sir … if the doorbell should ring.—

scenes.title: Maid
scenes.reentry: But, Sir … look … it is so light…

scenes.title: Maid
scenes.reentry: Mr. Alfred…

scenes.title: Maid
scenes.reentry: (*Covering her face*) Oh, my, I didn’t know that Mr. Alfred could be so wicked.

scenes.title: Young Man
scenes.reentry: I *saw* lots then … *that* … and *that* … that … and—

scenes.title: Oh, Mr. Alfred!
scenes.reentry: Young MAN

scenes.title: Maid
scenes.reentry: But if the doorbell should ring now—

scenes.title: Young Man
scenes.reentry: Confound it… What a noise that fellow makes—Perhaps he rang before, and we didn’t notice it.

scenes.title: Maid
scenes.reentry: Oh, no. I was listening all the while.

scenes.title: Maid
scenes.reentry: Mr. Alfred … you are … no … such a bad man.

scenes.title: Young Man
scenes.reentry: (*Opens the blinds quickly*)

scenes.title: Young Man
scenes.reentry: (*Annoyed*) Thank you.

scenes.title: Young Man
scenes.reentry: (*Evading her*) Listen, Marie,—I’m going to the café now.

scenes.title: Young Man
scenes.reentry: (*Formally*) I am going to the café now… If Dr. Schueller should call—

scenes.title: Young Man
scenes.reentry: (*Severely*) If Dr. Schueller should come, I—I am in the café.

scenes.title: The Young Man and the Young Wife
scenes.place: The Young Man and the Young Wife
scenes.reentry: *Evening—A drawing-room furnished with cheap elegance in a house in Schwind street. The Young MAN has just come in; and, still wearing his hat and overcoat, he lights the gas. Then he opens a door to a side-room and looks in. The light from

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: (*Heavily veiled, closes the door behind her, pausing a moment with her left hand over her heart, as though mastering a strong emotion*)

scenes.title: Young Man
scenes.reentry: (*Goes toward her, takes her left hand, and presses a kiss on the white glove with black stitching. He says softly.*) Thank you.

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: Alfred—Alfred!

scenes.title: Come, Madame… Come, Emma…
scenes.reentry: Young Wife

scenes.title: Young Man
scenes.reentry: (*Standing before her, holding her hand*)

scenes.title: Young Man
scenes.reentry: With me.

scenes.title: Young Man
scenes.reentry: Why terrible? It is a very proper house.

scenes.title: Young Man
scenes.reentry: Acquaintances of yours?

scenes.title: Young Man
scenes.reentry: But, Madame—You surely know your friends!

scenes.title: Young Man
scenes.reentry: But even had they been your best friends—they couldn’t possibly have recognized you… I, myself … if I didn’t know it was you … this veil—

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: There are two.

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: What are you thinking of, Alfred? I promised you: Five minutes… Not a moment more … I swear it, no more—

scenes.title: Young Man
scenes.reentry: Well, then, your veil—

scenes.title: Young Man
scenes.reentry: Very well, both of them—you will at least let me see your face.

scenes.title: Young Man
scenes.reentry: (*Deeply hurt*) Emma! You ask me…

scenes.title: Young Man
scenes.reentry: You’re still wearing your fur-coat—really, you will catch cold.

scenes.title: Young Man
scenes.reentry: Permit me.

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: (*Permits it*)

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: What is the matter?

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: How is that?

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: And now … now let me go again. I have done what you asked me to do.

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: You promised me to be good.

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: It is stifling hot in this room.

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: Put it with my hat.

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: And now—good-by—

scenes.title: Emma—! Emma—!
scenes.reentry: Young Wife

scenes.title: Young Man
scenes.reentry: Not one yet!—

scenes.title: Young Man
scenes.reentry: It is now exactly a quarter past six.

scenes.title: Young Man
scenes.reentry: You can see your sister any time…

scenes.title: Young Man
scenes.reentry: Because … I adore you, Emma!

scenes.title: Young Man
scenes.reentry: Since I met you, to no one.

scenes.title: Young Man
scenes.reentry: But you had already promised me the day before yesterday.

scenes.title: Young Man
scenes.reentry: I didn’t receive any.

scenes.title: Young Man
scenes.reentry: It is better as it is.

scenes.title: Young Man
scenes.reentry: (*Seizes her, and covers her face with burning kisses*)

scenes.title: Young Man
scenes.reentry: One more kiss—one more.

scenes.title: Young Man
scenes.reentry: Shall I tell you something, Emma? It is now for the first time that I know what happiness is.

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: (*Sinks back into the armchair*)

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: (*Sighs deeply*)

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: Alfred—Alfred, what are you doing to me!

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: Oh, don’t remind me of them.

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: Do you remember the ball at the Manufacturers’ Club?

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: (*Looks at him with a hurt expression*)

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: Only a drop, but first give me a glass of water.

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: (*Follows him with her eyes*)

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: Where have you been?

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: Now I’m going to ask you something, Alfred—and you must tell me the truth.

scenes.title: Young Man
scenes.reentry: I swear—

scenes.title: Young Man
scenes.reentry: But, Emma—this house was built twenty years ago!—

scenes.title: Young Man
scenes.reentry: With me—here—Emma!—It’s not kind of you even to imagine such a thing.

scenes.title: Young Man
scenes.reentry: But what is wrong? What is the matter with you? What fault?

scenes.title: Young Man
scenes.reentry: (*With the water-bottle in his hand, shakes his head sadly*) Emma, if you only knew how you hurt me.

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: (*Pours a glass of cognac*)

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: Yes, I shall go.

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: But suppose you were like other young men?

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: How do you know that?

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: (*Pleased*) Yes.

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: (*Takes a candied pear from the table, and puts it into her mouth*)

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: (*Catches the hands of the Young Man that threaten to stray*) What are you doing, Alfred?… Is that the way you keep your promise?

scenes.title: Young Man
scenes.reentry: (*Swallows the pear, then, more daringly*) Life is so short.

scenes.title: Young Man
scenes.reentry: (*Mechanically*) Oh, yes.

scenes.title: Young Man
scenes.reentry: Come, come, you only, only…

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: What are you doing?

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: Is there another room?

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: We’d better stay in here.

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: You are so… O merciful Heaven, what are you doing with me!—Alfred!

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: So then wait, wait a little… (*Weakly*) Go… I’ll call you.

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: But you’ll tear everything.

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: I never wear a corset. Odilon[2] doesn’t wear any either. But you can unbutton my shoes.

scenes.title: Young Man
scenes.reentry: (*Unbuttons her shoes and kisses her feet*)

scenes.title: Young Man
scenes.reentry: It’ll be warm in a minute.

scenes.title: Young Man
scenes.reentry: (*Slightly hurt, to himself*) She ought not to have said that.

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: (*Tenderly*) Come, come, come!

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: It smells like violets here.

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: Alfred… Alfred!!!!

scenes.title: Emma…
scenes.reentry: Young MAN

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: Don’t mind.

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: No … don’t… You are nervous. Calm yourself first.

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: Stendhal?

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: No. Why do you ask me?

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: What kind of a story?

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: Yes.

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: Yes.

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: Yes.

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: And.—

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: Of course. Anyway, you know … you promised me to be good.

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: But no, I’m not laughing. That story of Stendhal’s is really interesting. I have always thought that only older people … or people who … you know, people who have lived fast…

scenes.title: Young Man
scenes.reentry: The idea! That has nothing to do with it. By the way, I had completely forgotten the prettiest of Stendhal’s stories. One of the cavalry officers went so far as to say that he stayed for three or even six nights… I don’t remember now—that i

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: Both?

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: But surely there are many who don’t weep.

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: Oh—I thought Stendhal said that all cavalry officers weep on such an occasion.

scenes.title: Young Man
scenes.reentry: Look here, now you are laughing at me.

scenes.title: Young Man
scenes.reentry: Well, it makes me nervous anyway… Besides I have the feeling that you are thinking about it all the time. That embarrasses me still more.

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: I’m not thinking of it at all.

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: Do you want still further proofs?

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: How so? Come, let me hold your sweet little head.

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: Do you love me?

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: But you needn’t cry about it.

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: To tell you that you shouldn’t cry…

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: You are nervous, sweetheart.

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: But you ought not to be. It is beautiful even that … that we are together like good comrades…

scenes.title: Young Man
scenes.reentry: Now you are beginning again.

scenes.title: Young Man
scenes.reentry: Emma!—You will leave me in this way!

scenes.title: Young Man
scenes.reentry: Five minutes more…

scenes.title: Young Man
scenes.reentry: Emma … my ador… …

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: My Alfred!

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: But now I’ve really got to go.

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: I must go home. It is much too late to see my sister. How late is it?

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: You might look at your watch.

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: Get it.

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: (*Jumps up quickly*) For heaven’s sake… Quick, Alfred, give me my stockings. What shall I say? They must be waiting for me at home … eight o’clock…

scenes.title: Young Man
scenes.reentry: When shall I see you again?

scenes.title: Never
scenes.reentry: Young MAN

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: Just for that reason. Give me my shoes.

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: My button-hook is in my bag. Please, be quick…

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: Alfred, this may cost us our lives.

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: What shall I say, if he asks me where I’ve been?

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: Oh, if I only could lie.

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: Everything for a man like you. Oh, come here … let me give you a last kiss. (*She embraces him*)—And now—leave me by myself, go in the other room.—I can’t dress, if you are around.

scenes.title: Young Man
scenes.reentry: (*Goes into the drawing-room, where he dresses. He eats some pastry and drinks a glass of cognac*)

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: (*Calls after a while*) Alfred!

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: Isn’t it better that we didn’t weep?

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: Oh, how difficult it will be now—if we should meet by chance in company?

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: Yes. You too?

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: Oh, I shall not go. What do you imagine?—I would… (*She enters the drawing-room fully dressed, and takes a piece of chocolate pastry*) sink through the floor.

scenes.title: Young Man
scenes.reentry: To-morrow at Lobheimer’s. That’s fine.

scenes.title: Young Man
scenes.reentry: Well, the day after to-morrow … here.

scenes.title: Young Man
scenes.reentry: At six…

scenes.title: Young Man
scenes.reentry: Yes, as many as you want. Well, the day after to-morrow, here at six o’clock. Please say “yes,” sweetheart.

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: … We’ll discuss that to-morrow night during the cotillion.

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: Don’t muss my hair again.

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: Good-by…

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: Don’t ask me … don’t ask me … it’s too terrible.—Why do I love you so?—Good-by—If I meet any one again on the stairway, I shall faint.—Ugh!

scenes.title: Young Man
scenes.reentry: (*Kisses her hand for the last time*)

scenes.title: (Exit)
scenes.reentry: Young MAN

scenes.title: The Young Wife and the Husband
scenes.place: The Young Wife and the Husband
scenes.reentry: *A comfortable bedroom. It is half past ten at night. The Wife is lying abed and reading. The Husband enters the room in a dressing gown.*

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: (*Without looking up*) You have stopped working?

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: Well?—

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: (*Looking up*) Really?

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: (*Closing the book*) What’s the matter with you?

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: One might almost forget it sometimes.

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: Why?

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: Oh…

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: That’s beyond me.

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: I haven’t counted them!

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: Ah … do you mean that?

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: I, too.

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: Oh.

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: Run into months.

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: And now … now it seems we are at the end of another such period of friendship—?

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: (*Pressing her tenderly to him*) So it might seem.

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: You couldn’t. You are the wisest and most delicious being in the world. I am very happy to have found you.

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: You know how to make love very well—every now and then.

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: (*Laughing*) Oh!

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: Tell me—what kind of creatures are they?

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: But—this pity—it doesn’t seem quite appropriate to me.

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: Do all of them really sell themselves?

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: But why are they to be pitied?—They seem to enjoy themselves.

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: (*Cuddling to him*) It seems pleasant to fall.

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: Of course, Karl, of course. I was just thinking. Go on, tell me more. I like it when you talk like this. Tell me something.

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: What?—

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: The idea!

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: Why does that interest you?

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: You surely don’t think I have such bad taste, as to—No, Emma … it would be like a profanation.

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: And yet you have … heaven knows how many other women you have held in your arms, just as you are holding me now.

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: Don’t say “women.” You are *the* woman.

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: That’s a nice way to talk … remember you are a mother … our little girl is sleeping in there…

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: (*Snuggling against him*) But I want a boy, too.

scenes.title: Emma!
scenes.reentry: Young Wife

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: Would you?…

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: (*Accommodating*) All right.

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: Why? What do you mean?

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: (*Slightly disconcerted*) What makes you think of a thing like that?

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: (*Seriously*) Do you know such a woman?

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: Is there, perhaps, such a woman among your friends?

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: Did any of your friends … women talk about a lot of things—alone among themselves—did any of them ever confess—?

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: (*Uncertainly*) No.

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: Suspect … oh … suspect.

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: No, indeed, Karl, most certainly not. When I think things over—I don’t believe there is any one.

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: No one?

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: Promise me something, Emma.

scenes.title: Well?
scenes.reentry: Husband

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: And you think it necessary for me to promise that?

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: Do they?

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: Why?

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: Yes, of course. You are right.

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: Pleasure.

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: Well,—there must be something in it—! Otherwise, they wouldn’t do it.

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: (*Pensively*) An intoxication…

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: Well … it has happened to you, hasn’t it?

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: Who was she? Tell me! Do I know her?

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: Was it long ago? Was it very long before you married me?

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: But, Karl!

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: Are you in earnest?

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: Did you love her very much?

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: Then why…

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: Really?

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: Karl!

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: Karl!

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: Do you know what I am thinking of to-night?

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: Of … of … of Venice.

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: Yes…

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: You love me as much to-day.

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: Oh … if you would always…

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: My Karl!

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: Well, yes.

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: Then I would always know that you love me.

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: True!

scenes.title: Young Wife
scenes.reentry: Good-night!

scenes.title: The Husband and the Sweet Young Miss
scenes.place: The Husband and the Sweet Young Miss
scenes.reentry: *A private dining-room in the Riedhof, comfortably furnished with moderately good taste. A gas-grate is burning. The Husband and the Sweet Young Miss are disclosed. The remains of dinner are on the table, cream-cakes, fruit, cheese. In the

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: (*Is smoking a Havana cigar, and leaning against the corner of a sofa*)

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: Is it good?

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: Do you want another?

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: Your wine is all gone.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: No … stop. I’ll leave it anyway.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Am I?—Well, it takes time to get acquainted.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Right away… I’m not ready yet.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: What’s the matter?

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: (*Kissing him*) You are … excuse me, you have a lot of nerve.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Oh, no, I knew that long ago … from the first, in the street.—You must—

scenes.title: What?
scenes.reentry: Miss

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: Why?

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: Well, you can hardly say “right away.”

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: Do you think so?

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: Of course.

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: Besides, it’s much too cold for walking.

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: But here it’s nice and warm, isn’t it?

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: (*Weakly*) Don’t.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Certainly. Several blocks before you spoke to me.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: A lot of people follow me.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Guess … do you know what happened to me the other day? My cousin’s husband followed me in the dark, and didn’t recognize me.

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: Did he speak to you?

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: But they sometimes do, don’t they?

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: Well, and what do you do?

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: Hm-m … but you answered me.

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: (*Kisses her violently*) Your lips taste like cream-cakes.

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: I suppose many have told you that?

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: Now, be honest. How many have kissed this mouth before?

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: Why not?

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: All right, I’ll guess—but you mustn’t get angry!

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: Well, then, I’ll guess … twenty.

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: Oh, I was just guessing.

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: Say—ten.

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: Don’t be childish. Whether we walk about in the streets or sit in a room… We are in a restaurant. The waiter may come in at any moment—it doesn’t signify anything at all…

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: That’s just what I thought.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: If I must tell the truth—yes.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: But it wasn’t—no it wasn’t the way you imagine. I was in a private dining-room with a friend and her fiancé, once during the carnival.

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: It wouldn’t have been anything tragic, if you had ever gone—with your sweetheart—

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Of course, it wouldn’t have been anything serious. But I haven’t any sweetheart.

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: Oh, come now.

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: But you don’t expect to make me believe that I…

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: I see… But before then? Who was he?

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: I am curious because I love you.

scenes.title: Really?
scenes.reentry: Husband

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: What do you want me to tell?

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: (*Laughing*) Just a man.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: He looked something like you.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: If you hadn’t looked so much like him—

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Now, don’t ask, don’t you see that…

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Yes, that’s it.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: If I were you, I’d be pleased.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: You also remind me of him the way you speak … and the way you look at one…

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: What was he?

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: What was his name?

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: (*Embraces her. A long, burning kiss*)

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: Why do you want to leave me?

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: Later.

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: You live with your mother?

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: So—with your mother. Do you live alone with her?

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: Don’t sit so far away from me. Are you the oldest?

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: Where do you work?

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: Always?

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: Of course,—and what do you tell your mother, when you—come home so late?

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: Well, to-day, for example. Your mother will ask you, won’t she?

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: And what do you tell her?

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: Does she believe that?

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: Where did you get the tickets?

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: Oh, yes, a hairdresser … at the theater, I suppose?

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: Because I am interested. What does your other brother do?

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: And you also have a little sister?

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: Really?

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: And what did you do?

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: Are you as strict as all that?

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: You are a dear, sweet girl! (*Kisses her, and grows more tender*) You also remind me of some one.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: So—of whom?

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: How old are you?… You … why … I don’t even know your name.

scenes.title: Karl
scenes.reentry: Miss

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: Was his name also Karl?

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: And who was he?—You haven’t told me yet.

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: Did you love him very much?

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: I know what he was—a lieutenant.

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: (*Kisses her*) You have gray eyes. I thought, at first, they were black.

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: (*Kisses her eyes*)

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: (*More tenderly still*) No, indeed.

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: How old are you?—eighteen—isn’t it?

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: Nineteen … and I—

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: And a little more—Don’t let’s talk about it.

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: How long ago was that?

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: What makes you think so?

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: Then hold tight to me. So… (*He holds her close to him, and becomes more and more tender. She hardly resists*) I’ll tell you something, dear, we might go now.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Yes … home.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: What do you mean?… O, no—no… I won’t go anywhere else. What do you think I am?

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: But listen to me, child—the next time we meet, you know, we will arrange it so that … (*He has slipped to the floor with his head in her lap*) This is so comfy, oh, so comfy!

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: What are you doing? (*She kisses his hair*) Something must have been in that wine—I’m so sleepy … what would happen, if I couldn’t get up again? But, but—look, but Karl … if some one should come in … please … the waiter.

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: No … waiter … will ever come in … here…

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: (*Leaning with closed eyes in the corner of the sofa*)

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: (*Looking for a long time at the girl; speaking to himself*) Who knows what sort of a person she really is—Confound it … so quickly … that wasn’t very cautious of me … hm-m…

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: (*Without opening her eyes*) There must have been something in the wine.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Otherwise…

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Where are you? Why do you stay so far away? Come to me.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Now tell me if you really love me.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Listen… There must have … come, tell me the truth, what was in the wine.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Well, see, I can’t understand it. I’m really not that kind… We’ve known each other only since… Dear, I’m not that kind … honestly, I’m not—if you think that of me—

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: Well—why worry about that? I don’t think anything bad of you. I only think that you love me.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Yes…

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: I merely said it to say something.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: (*Almost defiantly*) Because I was ashamed.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Yes.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Yes, yes…

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: There weren’t any.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Oh, please, don’t tease me.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: No, thanks.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Well?

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Really?

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Do you really want to send me home?

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: You are quite changed. What have I done to you?

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: And it was only your looks, believe me, or you would have had to wait … many men have asked me to go with them to a private dining-room.

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: Well, would you like … to come here again with me soon … or rather somewhere else?

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: I don’t know.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Well, why don’t you make a date?

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Oh, you’re not a Viennese?

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Where?

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Oh, don’t be frightened, I won’t come to see you.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Honestly?

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: You are married, aren’t you?

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: I just got the impression.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Well, I would rather that you were single.—So you are married!—

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: If a man says he doesn’t live in Vienna, and he doesn’t always have time—

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: But that’s not so improbable.

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: And wouldn’t it hurt your conscience to have caused a married man to become unfaithful?

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Oh, my, no doubt your wife acts just like you.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: I thought you didn’t have a wife.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: But Karl, Karl, what is the matter? Are you angry? I really didn’t know that you were married. I was just talking. Come, don’t be angry.

scenes.title: Husband
scenes.reentry: (*Comes back to her after a few minutes*) You are strange creatures, you … women.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Stop … don’t … it’s too late now.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Would you?

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Oh, I can look out for myself.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Oh, my!

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Tell me, what do you think I am?

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: (*Snuggles up to him*)

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Yes.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Yes.

scenes.title: The Sweet Young Miss and the Poet
scenes.place: The Sweet Young Miss and the Poet
scenes.reentry: *A small room, furnished with taste and comfort. Red curtains half-darken the room. A large writing-table strewn with books and papers. A piano against the wall. The Sweet Young Miss and the Poet are disclosed. They are just entering. The P

scenes.title: Poet
scenes.reentry: (*Kisses her*) My darling!

scenes.title: Poet
scenes.reentry: Your eyes will have to get used to this semi-darkness.—Those sweet eyes—

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: But there won’t be time enough.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Because I can only stop a moment.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Just for the sake of a minute?

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: The idea!—I have to leave right away.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Riding, you mean.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: (*Laughing*) But I’m not tired at all!

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: One of yours.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: But I thought, Robert, you were a professor.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Because you said the piece you are playing is your own.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Of course … it must be beautiful … that’s the chief thing!—

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: By what?

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: (*Sleepily*) Of course I do.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: I’m not as stupid as that.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Go on, you are talking nonsense.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Indeed, it is. Won’t you play something else on the piano?

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: But hadn’t you better light the lamp?

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: I don’t know.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: What are you doing? (*She turns toward him*) What are you writing?

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: I’m not thirsty, but I am hungry.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Can’t you send somebody?

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Oh, really don’t bother; I have to go home anyway.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Oh, no. I haven’t time for that. And, then, where could we go? Somebody we know might see us.

scenes.title: Poet
scenes.reentry: Do you know such a lot of people?

scenes.title: Poet
scenes.reentry: Why trouble?

scenes.title: Poet
scenes.reentry: We can go somewhere, where no one can see us. There are plenty of restaurants with private dining-rooms.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: (*Singing*) “Let’s dine in a chambre separée!”

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: To tell the truth—yes.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Oh, it wasn’t the way you imagine… I went with a friend and her fiancé. They took me along.

scenes.title: Poet
scenes.reentry: And you expect me to believe that?

scenes.title: Poet
scenes.reentry: (*Close to her*) Did you blush? You can hardly see anything. I can’t even distinguish your features. (*He touches her cheeks with his hands*) But even so I recognize you.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Well, be careful that you don’t take me for some one else.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Thank you!

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: What are you talking about?

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Wouldn’t it be better to light the lamp?

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Very much … oh, so much!

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: I told you already that I didn’t.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: He was my fiancé.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Why … what’s the difference … look…

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: I’m sure people there wouldn’t be as wicked as you are.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Well?

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: My corset hurts me.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Yes. But you must behave.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: (*Rises, and takes off her corset in the darkness*)

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Yes, what is it?

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: What is the difference?

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Oh, you don’t write under your real name?

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Oh … stop … don’t.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: You are tearing my chemise.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Oh, Robert.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Tell me first—do you really love me?

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Robert … Robert…

scenes.title: Poet
scenes.reentry: It was heaven… My name is…

scenes.title: Poet
scenes.reentry: I call myself Biebitz.

scenes.title: Poet
scenes.reentry: My name is not Biebitz—I just use it as a pseudonym … well, don’t you recognize the name?

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: No.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: No really, I never heard it.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Oh, yes—I was at the opera only the other day with—you know, with one of my friends and her uncle, to hear Cavalleria Rusticana.

scenes.title: Poet
scenes.reentry: Hm, you don’t go then to see plays.

scenes.title: Poet
scenes.reentry: I’ll send you a ticket soon.

scenes.title: Poet
scenes.reentry: Oh … something funny … you don’t care to see anything sad?

scenes.title: Poet
scenes.reentry: Not even if it is a play of mine.

scenes.title: Poet
scenes.reentry: Let me light a candle now. I haven’t seen you since you have become my best beloved—Angel!

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Don’t. I’m ashamed. Give me a cover at least.

scenes.title: Later!
scenes.reentry: (*He approaches her with the light, and looks at her a long while*)

scenes.title: Poet
scenes.reentry: You are beautiful, you are Beauty itself. You are Nature herself. You are the simplicity which is holy.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Ouch! You are dropping wax on me. Look, why aren’t you more careful?

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Oh, pshaw, I don’t even know what you are talking about. I never heard of any Biebitz.

scenes.title: Poet
scenes.reentry: What is fame! No, forget what I have told you. Forget even the name. I am Robert and I want to remain Robert to you. I was only joking. (*Lightly*) I am not a writer at all. I’m a clerk, and in the evening I play the piano in a dancehall.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: But now I’m all mixed up … and the way you look at one. What is the matter, yes, what do you mean?

scenes.title: Poet
scenes.reentry: It is very strange—something that has never happened to me, sweetheart; I am on the verge of tears. You move me deeply. We ought to live together. Will you? We will be very much in love with each other.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Is it true about the dancehall?

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: How do you mean get away?

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: How absurd! How could I! What would mother say? And without me everything would be topsy-turvy at home in no time.

scenes.title: Poet
scenes.reentry: It would be so wonderful to live with you a few weeks, all alone with you, somewhere far away, in the forest, in the world of nature… Nature. And then, some day, “Good-by”—each going, without the other knowing where.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: You are talking already about saying good-by. And I thought that you loved me such a lot.

scenes.title: Poet
scenes.reentry: That is just the reason—(*Bends over her, and kisses her upon the forehead.*) You sweet darling!

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Please, hold me tight. I feel so cold.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: (*Rising*) Don’t look this way.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: What do you mean?

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Well, they might be better.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Come, have you a comb?

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Please … don’t!

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: But it is awfully late already.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Dear me, I must hurry. Please!

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: When would you like to see me?

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: What day is to-morrow?

scenes.title: Saturday
scenes.reentry: Miss

scenes.title: Poet
scenes.reentry: Then Sunday … hm … Sunday … on Sunday … now I’ll have to explain something to you.—I’m not Biebitz, but Biebitz is a friend of mine. I’ll introduce him to you sometime. Biebitz’s play will be given Sunday. I’ll send you tickets, and take yo

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Here you are talking about this Biebitz again.—I don’t understand what it is all about.

scenes.title: Poet
scenes.reentry: I won’t know you really, until I know what impression the play made on you.

scenes.title: Miss
scenes.reentry: Now … I’m ready.

scenes.title: The Poet and the Actress
scenes.reentry: *A room in an inn in the country. It is an evening in spring; moonlight floods the meadows and hills; the windows are open. A deep silence reigns. The Poet and the Actress enter, and as they cross the threshold, the candle which the Poet is

scenes.title: Poet
scenes.reentry: Oh…

scenes.title: Poet
scenes.reentry: The candle.—But we don’t need any. Look, how light it is. Wonderful!

scenes.title: Poet
scenes.reentry: What’s the matter with you?

scenes.title: Poet
scenes.reentry: (*Going to her*) What are you doing?

scenes.title: Poet
scenes.reentry: Do you believe in God?

scenes.title: Poet
scenes.reentry: Oh, I see!

scenes.title: Poet
scenes.reentry: (*Kneels beside her, and puts his arm around her waist*)

scenes.title: Poet
scenes.reentry: To God, I suppose.

scenes.title: Poet
scenes.reentry: Then why did you look out of the window?

scenes.title: Poet
scenes.reentry: But, child, it was your idea. You wanted to go to the country—and picked out this very place.

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: Well, wasn’t I right?

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: Isn’t it? If you had any real talent, this place might inspire you to write.

scenes.title: Poet
scenes.reentry: Have you been here before?

scenes.title: Poet
scenes.reentry: With whom?

scenes.title: Poet
scenes.reentry: Oh, really!

scenes.title: Poet
scenes.reentry: You’ve told me all about that already.

scenes.title: Poet
scenes.reentry: You bore me?… You can’t imagine what you mean to me… You are a whole world in itself… You are divine, you are a genius… You are the simplicity which is holy… Yes, you… But you oughtn’t to talk about Dick now.

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: That was merely a slip! Well!—

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: Come, give me a kiss!

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: But now we had better say good night. Good night, darling!

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: I mean, I am going to lie down and go to sleep.

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: There are surely a lot of other rooms in this house.

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: Yes.

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: Don’t talk nonsense, but just give me the bag from the table.

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: (*Takes a small framed picture out of the hand-bag and puts it on the dressing-table*)

scenes.title: Poet
scenes.reentry: What’s that?

scenes.title: Poet
scenes.reentry: Do you always carry her around with you?

scenes.title: Poet
scenes.reentry: You are joking? Can’t I help you?

scenes.title: Poet
scenes.reentry: And when may I return?

scenes.title: Poet
scenes.reentry: (*Kisses her*) Au revoir!

scenes.title: Poet
scenes.reentry: I shall walk up and down under your window. I love to wander about outdoors at night time. My finest inspirations come to me that way. And especially near you, under the breath of your longing, I might call it … entwined in your art.

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: You talk like an idiot…

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: Oh, well, but do go now. But don’t start to flirt with the waitress.—

scenes.title: (Goes)
scenes.reentry: Actress

scenes.title: Poet
scenes.reentry: (*Comes quickly upstairs and runs toward her. She in the meantime has gone to bed, and extinguished the light. He locks the door*)

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: So, now you may sit down beside me, and tell me a story.

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: Oh, no!

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: Tell me to whom you are unfaithful at this moment?

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: Well, if it’s any satisfaction to you, I am unfaithful to some one too.

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: And who do you suppose it is?

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: Guess, then.

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: My dear man, I’m not a chorus-girl.

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: Guess again.

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: Nonsense! He doesn’t care for women at all … didn’t you know that? He carries on with his postman!

scenes.title: Poet
scenes.reentry: No, really!—

scenes.title: Poet
scenes.reentry: (*Embraces her*)

scenes.title: Poet
scenes.reentry: Why do you torment me so?

scenes.title: Poet
scenes.reentry: I accept.

scenes.title: Poet
scenes.reentry: Yes … if I had had my way, I would have been there long ago… Listen…

scenes.title: What?
scenes.reentry: Poet

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: You are crazy, child, there are no crickets here.

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: Hurry up.

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: Now lie quite still… Sh … don’t move…

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: You would rather like to have an affair with me?

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: There are many who would like that…

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: Then, come, my cricket! I shall call you “cricket” from now on.

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: Now, tell me, whom am I deceiving?

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: Child, you have softening of the brain.

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: Please don’t talk such magnificent nonsense.

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: That’s better than acting in idiotic plays… Don’t you think so?

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: You conceited puppy. I suppose you are thinking of one of your own plays again.

scenes.title: Poet
scenes.reentry: Yes, I am.

scenes.title: Poet
scenes.reentry: Well, then!

scenes.title: Poet
scenes.reentry: And you might also tell me now why you didn’t turn up the day before yesterday. There was absolutely nothing the matter with you.

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: Well, I wanted to annoy you.

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: You were over-bearing.

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: Everybody at the theater thinks you are.

scenes.title: Really
scenes.reentry: Actress

scenes.title: Poet
scenes.reentry: And what did they say?

scenes.title: Poet
scenes.reentry: Oh, I see.

scenes.title: Poet
scenes.reentry: Don’t think now of others. Let’s be happy that we are here together, and tell me that you love me.

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: What further proof can you want?

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: I like that! What else do you want?

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: No, I have loved only one.

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: Dick.

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: You are a mood of mine.

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: Well, tell me, aren’t you proud?

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: It seems to me that you have good reason to be.

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: Yes, because of that, my little cricket!—What about the chirping? Are they still chirping?

scenes.title: Poet
scenes.reentry: All the time. Don’t you hear them?

scenes.title: Poet
scenes.reentry: You are wrong. Frogs croak.

scenes.title: Poet
scenes.reentry: But this is not croaking, child, this is chirping.

scenes.title: Poet
scenes.reentry: Please don’t call me that. It gets on my nerves.

scenes.title: Poet
scenes.reentry: My name is Robert.

scenes.title: Poet
scenes.reentry: But won’t you please call me simply by my own name?

scenes.title: Poet
scenes.reentry: May I light a cigarette?

scenes.title: Poet
scenes.reentry: What performance?

scenes.title: Well
scenes.reentry: Poet

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: You are joking.

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: You missed something wonderful.

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: It was a sensation. The people actually grew pale.

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: Benno said: Child, you acted divinely.

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: Indeed I was. And do you know why? Because I felt such a longing for you.

scenes.title: Poet
scenes.reentry: A little while ago you said that you stayed away just to annoy me.

scenes.title: Poet
scenes.reentry: Rather high for a mood.

scenes.title: Poet
scenes.reentry: And Dick…?

scenes.title: The Actress and the Count
scenes.reentry: *The bedroom of the Actress, luxuriously furnished. It is midday. The curtains are still down; a candle is burning on the dressing-table. The Actress is disclosed in her four-poster bed. Many newspapers are strewn about on the cover. The Co

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: Ah, Count.

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: Please, come closer.

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: Please sit down, Count.

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: Nothing serious? I was on the verge of death.

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: It is very good of you to have taken the trouble to call.

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: It was a great triumph, wasn’t it?

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: Thanks, for the beautiful flowers.

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: (*Indicating with her eyes a large flower-basket, which stands on a little table near the window*) There they are.

scenes.title: Count
scenes.reentry: You were literally overwhelmed with flowers and wreaths yesterday.

scenes.title: Count
scenes.reentry: (*Kissing her hand*) How sweet of you.

scenes.title: Count
scenes.reentry: But, Mademoiselle.

scenes.title: Count
scenes.reentry: You are a strange being … a sort of a problem almost—

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: Miss Birken, I suppose, is much less of a problem.

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: Oh!

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: Really?

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: From now on, I suppose, you will dine earlier.

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: Are there any pleasures left to an old man like you?

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: Do you think so?

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: Yes … thinking is a misfortune.

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: What do you mean by “up there”?

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: And what did you do in Hungary?

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: Yes, but why did you stay in Hungary so long?

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: But it must be enough to drive one mad.

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: Please go on; they are delightful!

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: Down there in Hungary, I suppose.

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: Like them—? I hate them! I hate to look at them. I never see any one. I’m always alone. Nobody enters my house.

scenes.title: Count
scenes.reentry: You see, I sort of thought that you hated people. It must often be the case with artists. If one lives in the higher regions… Well, you are lucky, you know at least why you live!

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: Who told you that? I haven’t the slightest notion what I’m living for!

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: Does that mean happiness?

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: I suppose you are right.

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: (*Grandly*) It is over.

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: (*Nods with wide open eyes*) It seems, you have grasped the essence of things.

scenes.title: Count
scenes.reentry: And, you see, when you have once clearly grasped this, it really doesn’t matter whether you live in Vienna or in the Puszta[3] or in Steinamanger.[4] You see, for instance … where may I put my cap? Yes, thank you … what were we talking abou

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: About the Puszta.

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: And what about love?

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: Like Miss Birken, for example.

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: But she’s your mistress, isn’t she?

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: Everybody knows it.

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: But you fought a duel on her account!

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: You are a gentleman, won’t you sit closer to me?

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: Here. (*She draws him to her, and passes her hand through his hair*) I knew you would come to-day.

scenes.title: Count
scenes.reentry: How did you know?

scenes.title: Count
scenes.reentry: You saw me from the stage, then?

scenes.title: Count
scenes.reentry: No, really?

scenes.title: Count
scenes.reentry: As on wings? On my account? I hadn’t the slightest suspicion that you noticed me!

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: Your aristocratic reserve is enough to drive one to despair.

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: “But”!… At least, take your saber off!

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: And now give me a kiss.

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: It would have been better if I had never seen you.

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: Count, you are a poseur!

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: Can’t you imagine how happy many a man would be if he were in your place!

scenes.title: Count
scenes.reentry: I’m perfectly happy.

scenes.title: Count
scenes.reentry: I told you, Mademoiselle, you are a problem.

scenes.title: Count
scenes.reentry: Well then, may I ask (*kissing her hand*) that I may call again this evening?

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: This evening … but I have to act then.

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: And you ask for nothing else?

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: (*Hurt*) You can beg a long while then, you abominable poseur.

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: It does not open from the outside.

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: Possibly!…

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: Well—you are about the worst case of lunacy I have ever met!

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: Oh, but you are a darling!

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: How do you imagine it?

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: I am not Miss Birken.

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: And then?

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: Do sit closer. Closer.

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: It’s very warm in here, don’t you think so?

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: Oh, Count, that is contrary to your program.

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: (*Drawing him close to her*)

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: Do you think so? And so dark, just as if it were evening… (*Draws him toward her*) It is evening … it is night… Close your eyes, if there is too much light for you. Come!… Come!…

scenes.title: Count
scenes.reentry: (*Offers no further resistance*)

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: And what about atmosphere now, you poseur?

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: What a thing to say!

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: You should have been an actor! Really! You understand women! And do you know, what I shall do now?

scenes.title: Count
scenes.reentry: Well?

scenes.title: Count
scenes.reentry: But why?

scenes.title: Count
scenes.reentry: But…

scenes.title: Count
scenes.reentry: I shall never forget it!

scenes.title: Count
scenes.reentry: What do you mean?

scenes.title: Count
scenes.reentry: Oh, yes, let’s say, the day after to-morrow.

scenes.title: Count
scenes.reentry: There wouldn’t be much sense in that.

scenes.title: Count
scenes.reentry: You don’t quite understand me. What I mean has rather to do, how shall I express myself, rather concerns the soul.

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: What concern of mine is your soul?

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: Don’t bother me with your philosophy. If I want any of that, I can read books.

scenes.title: Count
scenes.reentry: One never learns from books.

scenes.title: Count
scenes.reentry: Well, then, if I may, I shall wait in my carriage…

scenes.title: Count
scenes.reentry: … After the play.

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: What are you doing?

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: Well, this evening it shall be a formal call.

scenes.title: Actress
scenes.reentry: I’ll take care of that. And now give me a last kiss, you darling little philosopher. Here, you seducer, you … sweet child, you seller of souls, you … panther. (*After she has ardently kissed him several times, she thrusts him violently away

scenes.title: Count
scenes.reentry: Not at all, mademoiselle! (*At the door*) Au revoir.

scenes.title: The Count and the Girl of the Streets
scenes.place: The Count and the Girl of the Streets
scenes.reentry: *It is morning toward six o’clock. A poorly furnished room with one window. The dirty yellowish blinds are down. Tattered, greenish curtains. On the dresser are several photographs, and beside them a cheap woman’s hat of conspicuously bad t

scenes.title: Count
scenes.reentry: (*Stirs, rubs his eyes, sits up suddenly, remains seated, and looks around*) Where am I?… Oh, yes … I actually went home with the woman, it seems… (*He rises quickly, notices her bed*) Oh, there she is… Queer, what sort of things can happen

scenes.title: Girl
scenes.reentry: (*Awakening*) Well … who’s there so early in the morning—? (*Recognizing him*) Good morning, sonny!

scenes.title: Count
scenes.reentry: Good morning. Have a good sleep?

scenes.title: Count
scenes.reentry: (*Bends down to her, considers, and draws back*) I was just going…

scenes.title: Going?
scenes.reentry: Count

scenes.title: Girl
scenes.reentry: You want to go away?

scenes.title: Girl
scenes.reentry: Well, good-by, you’ll come some other time.

scenes.title: Girl
scenes.reentry: (*Reaches out her hand from under the cover*)

scenes.title: Girl
scenes.reentry: Why do you look at me that way?

scenes.title: Girl
scenes.reentry: Yes, the lamps are always a nuisance.

scenes.title: Girl
scenes.reentry: Well, what would you guess?

scenes.title: Girl
scenes.reentry: Oh, of course!

scenes.title: Older?
scenes.reentry: Girl

scenes.title: Count
scenes.reentry: And how long have you been…

scenes.title: Count
scenes.reentry: You began early.

scenes.title: Count
scenes.reentry: (*Sits down upon her bed*) Tell me, are you really happy?

scenes.title: Count
scenes.reentry: I mean, are things going well with you?

scenes.title: Count
scenes.reentry: Yes… Well, did it never occur to you that you might become something else?

scenes.title: Girl
scenes.reentry: What might I become?

scenes.title: Girl
scenes.reentry: Do you imagine I haven’t any?

scenes.title: Girl
scenes.reentry: I don’t go with everybody. Thank heaven, I don’t have to. I pick those I want.

scenes.title: Count
scenes.reentry: (*Looks around the room*)

scenes.title: Count
scenes.reentry: We? Who?

scenes.title: Count
scenes.reentry: There are others—

scenes.title: Count
scenes.reentry: I hear some one snoring.

scenes.title: Count
scenes.reentry: What an awful life!

scenes.title: Count
scenes.reentry: What do you do on the streets at noon?

scenes.title: Count
scenes.reentry: Oh, yes … of course… (*Rises, takes out his wallet, and puts a banknote on the table*) Good-by!

scenes.title: Girl
scenes.reentry: Going already… Good-by… Call again soon.

scenes.title: Count
scenes.reentry: (*Stands still*) Tell me, is everything a matter of indifference to you already?

scenes.title: Girl
scenes.reentry: What?

scenes.title: Girl
scenes.reentry: (*Yawning*) I want to sleep.

scenes.title: Girl
scenes.reentry: Why do you ask?

scenes.title: Girl
scenes.reentry: Do I look like some one?

scenes.title: Girl
scenes.reentry: Well…

scenes.title: Girl
scenes.reentry: You talk just like Frank.

scenes.title: Girl
scenes.reentry: The waiter in our café.

scenes.title: Girl
scenes.reentry: He is also always telling me I might make my fortune, and wanting me to marry him.

scenes.title: Count
scenes.reentry: Why don’t you?

scenes.title: Count
scenes.reentry: The eyes … the very same eyes… Bobby would surely call me a fool.—But I must kiss your eyes once more … so … and now God bless you, now I must go.

scenes.title: Girl
scenes.reentry: Good-by…

scenes.title: Girl
scenes.reentry: At what?

scenes.title: Girl
scenes.reentry: There are many men who aren’t in the mood in the morning.

scenes.title: Girl
scenes.reentry: (*With closed eyes*) All right.

scenes.title: Girl
scenes.reentry: I’m always at home. You only have to ask for Leocadia.

scenes.title: Girl
scenes.reentry: What way?

scenes.title: Girl
scenes.reentry: In the morning?

scenes.title: Girl
scenes.reentry: No, that has never happened to me.

scenes.title: Girl
scenes.reentry: Why shouldn’t you like me? You liked me well enough by night.

scenes.title: Girl
scenes.reentry: But you liked me better last night.

scenes.title: Girl
scenes.reentry: Why ask such foolish questions?

scenes.title: Girl
scenes.reentry: Certainly … with me.

scenes.title: Girl
scenes.reentry: Yes, don’t you remember?

scenes.title: Girl
scenes.reentry: But you fell asleep right away.

scenes.title: Girl
scenes.reentry: Yes, sonny. But you must have been terribly drunk, that you don’t remember.

scenes.title: Count
scenes.reentry: So… And yet … there is a faint resemblance… Good-by… (*Listens*) … What is the matter?

scenes.title: Girl
scenes.reentry: The servant is up. Give her a tip as you go out. The outside door is open, so you won’t have to give anything to the janitor.

scenes.title: Count
scenes.reentry: (*In the anteroom*) Well… It would have been beautiful, if I had kissed her only on the eyes. It would have been almost an adventure… But it wasn’t my destiny. (*The servant opens the door*) Ah—here… Good-night.—

scenes.title: Servant
scenes.reentry: Good morning!

scenes.title: Footnotes
scenes.reentry: [1] The Luna Park of Vienna.

breaths.text: What business is that of yours? Is it far?
That’s too far for me. Give me a kiss.
(*Kissing him*) I like that best anyway—when I love some one.
I don’t. No, I can’t go with you. It’s too far.
Look here—if my place is too far to-night—there … there…
It’s nice and quiet there, too … no one is around.
Oh, that’s not the real thing.
It’s always the real thing with me. Come, stay with me now. Who knows, if we’ll be alive to-morrow.
Be careful! It’s dark here. If you slip, you’ll fall in the river.
Would be the best thing, perhaps.
Sh-h. Wait a minute. We’ll come to a bench soon.
You seem to know this place pretty well.
I’d like to have you for a sweetheart.
I’d cure you of that soon enough.
Don’t make so much noise. Sometimes a guard stumbles down here. Would you believe we are in the middle of Vienna?
You are crazy! If we slipped here, we’d fall into the river.
It would have been nicer on the bench.
Here or there, it doesn’t matter to me… Well, pick yourself up.
I must get to the barracks. I’ll be late anyhow.
Humph! I never heard such a name before.
Give me just a dime for the janitor.
Humph!… Do you think I’m your meal-ticket? Good-by, Leocadia…

*Prater Gardens. Sunday Evening. A road which leads from the Wurstelprater[1] into dark tree arcades. Confused music from the Wurstelprater can still be heard; also strains from the cheap dancehall, a vulgar polka, played by a brass band. THE Soldier. THE Parlor-Maid.*
Now tell me why you wanted to leave.
It was so beautiful and I so love to dance.
(*Submitting*) But we aren’t dancing now. Why do you hold me so tight?
You’ve always got a “Katy” on your mind.
Goodness, it’s dark here. I’m afraid.
You needn’t be afraid when I’m with you. I can take care of myself!
But where are we going? There’s no one around. Come, let’s go back!… It’s so dark!
(*Pulling at his cigar until it glows brightly*) There … it’s already getting brighter. Ha—! Oh, you dearie!
Oh! what are you doing there? If I had known this before!
The devil take me, if any one at the dance to-day felt softer and rounder than you, Miss Marie.
Did you find it out in the same way with all the others?
You notice things … dancing. You find out lots that way!
But you danced much oftener with that cross-eyed blonde than with me.
She’s an old friend of one of my pals.
Of the corporal with the upturned mustache?
Oh no, I mean the civilian. You know, the one who was talking with me at the table in the beginning. The one who has such a husky voice.
Did he do anything to you? I’ll show him! What did he do to you?
Oh nothing… I only noticed how he was with the others.
You’ll burn me with your cigar.
Pardon me!—Miss Marie—or may I say Marie?
We’re not such good friends yet…
There’re many who don’t like each-other, and yet use first names.
Next time, if we… But, Frank!
That’s right, call me Frank, Miss Marie.
Don’t be so fresh—but, sh-h, suppose some one should come!
What if some one did come? They couldn’t see anything two steps off.
For goodness’ sake, where are we going?
Look! There’s two just like us.
Why do you say: “two like us”—
Well, I mean, they like each other too.
Look out! What’s that there? I nearly fell.
Don’t shove me so. I’ll fall.
Stop! Now I’m really going to scream—What are you doing?… Stop now—
Then, let’s go back where the people are.
We don’t need them. Why—Marie, we need … for that…
Stop, Frank, please, for Heaven’s sake! Listen to me, if I had … known … oh … come!
… I can’t see your face at all.
Well, Miss Marie, you can’t stay here on the grass all night.
Well, what’s the matter with me?
Yes, yes. Say, wait a minute.
Why do you leave me alone?
Can’t you let me light my cigar!
It’ll be light again to-morrow morning.
Tell me, at least, you love me.
Well, you must have felt that, Miss Marie!
Well, what’s wrong? I don’t like to walk around in the dark.
Tell me, Frank … do you love me?
But I just told you that I loved you!
Won’t you give me a little kiss?
Would you really like to go back, and dance again?
But, Frank, see, I have to get home. Madame will scold me anyway,—she’s cranky … she’d like it best if I never went out.
But, I thought, Frank, you’d take me home.
Please, it’s so sad to go home alone.
So? Then we go the same way … but it’s still too early for me … me for the dance… I’ve got late leave to-day… I don’t need to be back at the barracks before twelve o’clock. I’m going to dance.
Oh, I see, now it’s that cross-eyed blonde’s turn.
Oh Lord, how wicked men are. I’m sure you do the same to every one.
Please, Frank, no more to-day—stay with me to-day, you see—
Oh, very well, all right. But I suppose I may dance.
I’m not going to dance with any one else to-night.
The hall! How quick we got back. They’re still playing the same thing … that tatata-tum tatata-tum (*He hums with the band*)… Well, I’ll take you home, if you want to wait for me … if not … good-by—
Say, Miss Marie, get yourself a glass of beer. (*Turning to a blonde who is just dancing past him in the arms of another, very formally*) Miss, may I ask for a dance?—

*Sultry summer afternoon. The parents of the Young MAN are away in the country. The cook has gone out. The Parlor-Maid is in the kitchen writing a letter to the soldier who is now her sweetheart. The Young MAN’S bell rings. She gets up and goes to his room. The Young MAN is lying on a couch, smoking a cigarette and reading a French novel.*
Oh, yes, Marie, oh, yes; I rang, yes … I only wanted … yes, of course… Oh, yes, of course, let the blinds down, Marie… It’s cooler with the blinds down … yes…
(*The Maid goes to the window and pulls down the blinds*)
(*Continues reading*) What are you doing, Marie? Oh, yes. But, now, I can’t see to read.
You are always so studious, Sir.
(*Tries to go on with his reading, lets the book fall, and rings again*)
I say, Marie … let’s see, what was it I wanted to say? … oh, yes… Is there any cognac in the house?
Well, then ask Lini for it.
Yes, but it’s Lini’s day out.
Can I get anything for you from the café, Sir?
Thank you, no… It is hot enough as it is. I don’t need any cognac. Listen, Marie, bring me a glass of water. Wait, Marie,—let it run, till it gets quite cold.

*Exit Maid. The Young MAN gazes after her. At the door the Maid looks back at him, and the Young MAN glances into the air. The Maid turns on the water and lets it run. Meanwhile, she goes into her room, washes her hands, and arranges her curls before the mirror. Then she brings the glass of water to the Young MAN. She approaches the couch. The Young MAN raises himself upon his elbow. The Maid gives him the glass of water and their fingers touch.*
Thank you—Well, what is the matter?—Be careful. Put the glass back on the tray. (*He leans back, and stretches himself*) How late is it?
(*Goes. At the door she turns around. The Young MAN has followed her with his eyes; she notices it, and smiles*)
(*Remains stretched out awhile; then, suddenly, he gets up. He walks to the door, back again, and lies down on the couch. He again tries to read. After a few moments, he rings once more.*)
(*Appears with a smile which she does not try to hide*)
Listen, Marie, there was something I wanted to ask you. Didn’t Dr. Schueller call this morning?
No, Sir, nobody called this morning.
That is strange. Then, Dr. Schueller didn’t call. Do you know Dr. Schueller by sight?
Of course, I do. He’s the big gentleman with the black beard.
Yes. Then, perhaps, he called after all?
Still nearer … so … ah … I only thought…
I thought… Well, I thought—only about your blouse … what kind of a blouse is it … can’t you come closer. I won’t bite you.
(*Comes close to him*) What is the matter with my blouse? Don’t you like it, Sir?
(*Takes hold of her blouse, and draws her down to him*) Blue? It is a nice blue. (*Simply*) You are very prettily dressed, Marie.
Ah… What is the matter?… (*He has opened her blouse. In a matter of fact tone*) You have a beautiful white skin, Marie.
(*Kissing her on the breast*) That can’t hurt you.
But you sigh so. Why are you sighing?
And what charming little slippers you have…
… But … Sir … if the doorbell should ring.—
But, Sir … look … it is so light…
You needn’t feel at all shy with me. You needn’t feel shy with anybody … any one as pretty as you. Yes, really, you are, Marie… Do you know your hair actually smells sweet.
Don’t make such a fuss, Marie… Anyway, I’ve already seen you otherwise. When I came home the other night and went to get some water, the door to your room was open … well…
(*Covering her face*) Oh, my, I didn’t know that Mr. Alfred could be so wicked.
I *saw* lots then … *that* … and *that* … that … and—
But if the doorbell should ring now—
Now forget that … we simply wouldn’t open the door.
Confound it… What a noise that fellow makes—Perhaps he rang before, and we didn’t notice it.
Oh, no. I was listening all the while.
Well, see what’s the matter. Peek through the curtains.
Mr. Alfred … you are … no … such a bad man.
(*Returns*) He must have gone away again. Anyway, no one is there now. Perhaps, it was Dr. Schueller.
(*Evading her*) Listen, Marie,—I’m going to the café now.
(*Formally*) I am going to the café now… If Dr. Schueller should call—
He won’t come any more to-day.
(*Severely*) If Dr. Schueller should come, I—I am in the café.
(*He goes to the adjoining room. The Maid takes a cigar from the smoking-stand, puts it in her blouse and goes out.*)

*Evening—A drawing-room furnished with cheap elegance in a house in Schwind street. The Young MAN has just come in; and, still wearing his hat and overcoat, he lights the gas. Then he opens a door to a side-room and looks in. The light from the drawing-room shimmers over the inlaid floor as far as the Louis Quinze bed, which stands against the opposite wall. A reddish light plays from the fire-place in the corner of the bedroom upon the hangings of the bed. The Young MAN now inspects the bedroom. He takes an atomizer from the dressing-table, and sprays the bed-pillows with a fine rain of violet perfume. Then he carries the atomizer through both rooms, constantly pressing upon the bulb, so that soon the odor of violets pervades the place. He then takes off his hat and coat. He sits down in a blue velvet armchair, lights a cigarette, and smokes. After a short pause he rises again, and makes sure that the green shutters are closed.
